issues.display_title: Issue #470: Published Folder Bookmark Contributors API
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 17/07/26

✅ Implementation: Published Folder Bookmark Contributors API

Example API

Endpoint: GET /bookmark/published/:slug/contributors
Description: Retrieves unique contributor avatars for the avatar strip on published folder bookmark detail. The endpoint returns only avatars and the remaining unique contributor count.

Example cURL Request

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>/contributors" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=4"

Request Parameters

  • slug (string, required): Published folder bookmark slug.
  • limit (int, optional): Number of avatars to return. Defaults to 4.

Visibility Rules

  • Role viewer can access public published folder contributors.
  • Role user can access public published folder contributors.
  • Other roles return 401 Unauthorized.
  • All roles exclude:
    • deactivated users
    • private/non-public posts
    • unpublished posts
    • video360 posts
  • Role user also excludes:
    • blocked users
    • blocked posts

Data Source

This endpoint reads from:

public.views_published_folder_posts

Required view columns:

  • folder_slug
  • bookmark_created_at
  • slug
  • avatar
  • visibility
  • is_publish
  • post_type
  • encrypt

Success Response

If a folder has 20 unique contributors and the API returns 4 avatars, remaining_contributors is 16.

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Published Folder Bookmark Contributors",
    "avatars": [
      "https://example.com/avatar-1.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-2.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-3.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-4.jpg"
    ],
    "remaining_contributors": 16
  }
}

Empty Or Not Found Response

If no visible contributors are available for the requester, the endpoint returns 409.

{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "data": {
    "status": "Conflict",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Folder Not Found"
    }
  }
}

Unauthorized Response

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unauthorized",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Unauthorized"
    }
  }
}

FE Usage Example

Load folder header:

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false"

Load contributor avatars for the avatar strip:

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>/contributors" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=4"

Load posts:

curl -G "http://localhost:3000/bookmark/published/<slug>/posts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_token>" \
  -H "ec: false" \
  --data-urlencode "page=1" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10"

Summary

Added a separate endpoint for the published folder bookmark avatar strip. The endpoint returns only visible unique contributor avatars and the count of unique contributors not shown in the strip.

Endpoint

GET /bookmark/published/:slug/contributors?limit=4

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors.go
  • src/Controllers/V1/BookmarksControllers.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes_test.go
  • docs/tasks/07-published-folder-bookmark-contributors.md

Implementation Details

Route

Registered the contributors endpoint:

Bookmark.Get("/published/:slug/contributors", Controllers.PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors)

This keeps contributors separate from:

  • GET /bookmark/published/:slug
  • GET /bookmark/published/:slug/posts

Action

Created PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors in src/Action/V1/Bookmarks.

The handler:

  • Reads slug from route params.
  • Reads limit from query params.
  • Defaults limit to 4.
  • Supports role viewer and user.
  • Rejects unsupported roles with 401 Unauthorized.
  • Loads deactive users from Redis key:
    • <prefix>_deactive_users_ec
  • For role user, loads:
    • user data through UserFunctions.UserDatas
    • blocked users from <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>
    • blocked posts from <prefix>_blocked_post_ec_<encrypt>
  • Reuses publishedFolderPostsBaseQuery so visibility filters match the published folder posts endpoint.

Base query:

Config.DB.Table("views_published_folder_posts").
    Where("folder_slug = ?", folderSlug).
    Where("visibility = ?", "public").
    Where("is_publish = ?", true).
    Where("post_type != ?", "video360")

Additional filters:

if len(blockPost) != 0 {
    query.Where("slug NOT IN (?)", blockPost)
}

if len(notInEncrypt) != 0 {
    query.Where("encrypt NOT IN (?)", notInEncrypt)
}

Unique Contributors

Contributors are unique by encrypt.

Total unique contributors is counted in the database:

basePosts.Distinct("encrypt").Count(&totalContributors)

Avatar rows are limited in the database:

Select("avatar").
    Group("encrypt, avatar").
    Order("MAX(bookmark_created_at) DESC").
    Limit(limit)

The Go loop only maps the limited query result into a string slice. It does not load every bookmark into memory.

Remaining Contributors

The API returns the remaining contributor count, not the total count:

remainingContributors := totalContributors - int64(len(avatars))
if remainingContributors < 0 {
    remainingContributors = 0
}

Example:

  • total unique contributors: 20
  • returned avatars: 4
  • remaining_contributors: 16

Error Handling

If slug is empty:

400 Bad Request

If role is not user or viewer:

401 Unauthorized

If no visible contributors exist after filters:

409 Folder Not Found

If the database query fails:

500 Failed to get data

Encrypted Response

The handler preserves the existing ec: true response behavior used by related bookmark endpoints:

  • Builds the encrypted payload with Functions.EncryptResult.
  • Returns cry and ls.
  • Adds e4 for viewer.

Response Shape

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Published Folder Bookmark Contributors",
    "avatars": [
      "https://example.com/avatar-1.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-2.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-3.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-4.jpg"
    ],
    "remaining_contributors": 16
  }
}

Verification

Red test first:

go test ./src/Routes/V1 -run TestRegisterBookmarksRoutesAddsPublishedContributorsRoute -count=1

Expected failure before route registration:

expected GET route /bookmark/published/:slug/contributors to be registered

Final checks:

go test ./src/Routes/V1 -run TestRegisterBookmarksRoutesAddsPublishedContributorsRoute -count=1
go test ./...

Result: pass.

Goal

Create a separate endpoint for the avatar strip under published folder bookmark detail. The endpoint returns only unique contributor avatars and the count of remaining unique contributors not shown in the avatar strip.

Endpoint

GET /bookmark/published/:slug/contributors?limit=4

Requirements

  • Use a separate endpoint, not the folder detail endpoint and not the posts endpoint.
  • Read from views_published_folder_posts.
  • Contributors must be unique by user identity, using encrypt.
  • Response must only include avatar list and remaining contributor count.
  • limit defaults to 4.
  • remaining_contributors = total_unique_contributors - len(avatars), minimum 0.
  • Apply the same visibility rules as GET /bookmark/published/:slug/posts:
    • role must be user or viewer
    • only visibility = public
    • only is_publish = true
    • exclude post_type = video360
    • exclude deactivated users
    • for role user, exclude blocked users and blocked posts

Success Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "messages": "Published Folder Bookmark Contributors",
    "avatars": [
      "https://example.com/avatar-1.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-2.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-3.jpg",
      "https://example.com/avatar-4.jpg"
    ],
    "remaining_contributors": 16
  }
}

Empty Or Not Found Response

If no visible published posts are available for the requester, return 409 Folder Not Found, matching the published folder posts endpoint.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderBookmarkContributors.go
  • src/Controllers/V1/BookmarksControllers.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/BookmarksRoutes_test.go
  • docs/tasks/07-published-folder-bookmark-contributors.md

issues.display_title: Issue #391: Refactor Banned Support Module to Use GORM Models
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 17/07/26

✅ Implementation: Refactor Banned Support Module

This document tracks the execution details for the banned support endpoint GORM refactoring.

Phase 1: Banned User

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedUser.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import.
    • Replaced map-based users lookup with Models.User.
    • Replaced Config.DB.Table("users").Updates(...) calls with Config.DB.Model(&Models.User{}).Where(...).Updates(...).
    • Added explicit error handling for ban, no-violation, and restore update failures.
    • Updated restored-user email payload to read from typed Models.User fields.
    • Preserved existing validation, status handling, worker queue payloads, and response payloads.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 2: Banned Post

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedPost.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import.
    • Replaced map-based posts lookup with Models.Post.
    • Replaced Config.DB.Table("posts").Updates(...) calls with Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{}).Where(...).Updates(...).
    • Added explicit error handling for ban, no-violation, and restore update failures.
    • Preserved existing report status updates, worker queue payloads, and response payloads.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 3: Banned Comment

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedComment.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added the Models import.
    • Replaced map-based comment lookup with Models.Comment.
    • Replaced Config.DB.Table("comment").Updates(...) calls with Config.DB.Model(&Models.Comment{}).Where(...).Updates(...).
    • Added explicit error handling for ban, no-violation, and restore update failures.
    • Preallocated reporter payload slices and skipped empty reporter user IDs.
    • Preserved existing report status updates, worker queue payloads, and response payloads.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Verification

  • Ran go test ./src/Action/V1/Supports.
  • Result: passed with no test files.

Background

The support banned endpoints manage moderation status for users, posts, and comments. The main state updates already use GORM model updates, but report-status helpers still rely on raw SQL UPDATE ... RETURNING queries and local reporter row structs. Refactoring these helpers toward model-based operations will keep the banned module aligned with the wider GORM refactor while preserving the existing moderation workflow.

Objective

Refactor banned support endpoints to reduce raw SQL usage, use typed GORM models for report issue updates, and keep the existing worker queue payload behavior unchanged.

Scope

  • Refactor BannedUser report status update logic in src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedUser.go.
  • Refactor BannedPost report status update logic in src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedPost.go.
  • Refactor BannedComment report status update logic in src/Action/V1/Supports/BannedComment.go.
  • Add or update model fields for ReportIssueUser, ReportIssuePost, and ReportIssueComment if needed by the refactor.
  • Preserve the current ban, no-violation, and restore behavior.
  • Preserve worker queue payload fields and queue names.
  • Preserve existing response messages and validation behavior.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Banned user, post, and comment endpoints keep the same API request and response contracts.
  • Pending report rows are still updated from status 0 to the correct reviewed status.
  • Reporter payloads still include reporter user ID, category, and reported timestamp.
  • Worker publishing remains asynchronous through the existing RabbitMQ queues.
  • No behavior changes for already-banned, not-banned, not-found, or forbidden cases.
  • Verification passes with:
go test ./src/Action/V1/Supports

issues.display_title: Issue #392: Refactor User Social Relation APIs to Use GORM Models
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 17/07/26

✅ Implementation: Refactor User Social Relation APIs

This document tracks the execution details for the user social relation GORM refactoring.

Phase 1: Block User

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/BlockUser.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added imports for Models, uuid, and gorm.
    • Replaced map-based users lookup with Models.User.
    • Replaced map-based user_blocks lookup with Models.UserBlocks.
    • Replaced raw bookmark deletion with Config.DB.Delete(&Models.Bookmark{}, ...).
    • Replaced raw follower cleanup with Config.DB.Where(...).Delete(&Models.Followers{}).
    • Replaced raw user_blocks insert with Config.DB.Create([]Models.UserBlocks{...}) and explicit UUID generation.
    • Replaced raw unblock deletion with Config.DB.Where(...).Delete(&Models.UserBlocks{}).
    • Preserved existing bookmark counter updates, Redis refresh calls, ElasticSearch updates, slim response handling, and response messages.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 2: Follow User

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/FollowUser.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added imports for Models, uuid, and gorm.
    • Replaced map-based users lookup with Models.User.
    • Replaced string-based follower lookup with Models.Followers.
    • Replaced raw follower insert with Config.DB.Create(&Models.Followers{...}) and explicit UUID generation.
    • Replaced raw follower delete with Config.DB.Delete(&Models.Followers{}, ...).
    • Preserved existing check/follow/unfollow behavior, block validation, ElasticSearch updates, Redis refresh calls, slim response handling, and response messages.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Phase 3: Subscribe User

  • Target File:
    • src/Action/V1/Users/SubscribeUser.go
  • Changes Applied:
    • Added imports for Models, uuid, and gorm.
    • Replaced map-based users lookup with Models.User.
    • Replaced map-based follower lookup with Models.Followers.
    • Replaced raw subscribe update with Config.DB.Model(&Models.Followers{}).Where(...).Update(...).
    • Preserved existing subscribe/unsubscribe validation, not-following response, same-status response, block validation, and response messages.
  • Status: Completed & Compiled Successfully.

Verification

  • Ran go test ./src/Action/V1/Users.
  • Result: passed with no test files.

Background

The user social relation endpoints currently use direct table access and raw SQL for block, follow, and subscribe operations. These endpoints can use existing GORM models (Models.User, Models.UserBlocks, Models.Followers) to make relation checks and mutations type-safe while preserving existing API behavior.

Objective

Refactor the user block, follow, and subscribe endpoints to use GORM models for user lookup, relation lookup, creation, update, and deletion.

APIs to Refactor

  • BlockUser.go: Replace direct users and user_blocks table access plus raw SQL inserts/deletes with Models.User and Models.UserBlocks.
  • FollowUser.go: Replace direct users and followers table access plus raw SQL inserts/deletes with Models.User and Models.Followers.
  • SubscribeUser.go: Replace direct users and followers table access plus raw SQL updates with Models.User and Models.Followers.

Acceptance Criteria

  • No raw SQL INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE queries remain in the refactored endpoints.
  • Existing validation and response messages remain unchanged.
  • Self-block, not-found, already-followed, unfollow, subscribe, and unsubscribe behavior remains unchanged.
  • Redis cache updates for blocked users and blocked posts remain unchanged.
  • UUIDs are handled with existing model types instead of string-only row maps where possible.
  • Verification passes with:
go test ./src/Action/V1/Users
